cause.mopar: names 'Motor - Window Regulator', 'MOTOR Window Regulator', 'MOTOR WINDOW REGULATOR 6 Pin [Front]', 'MOTOR WINDOW REGULATOR 2 Pin [Rear]' (beside 'Window Motor'): positions.packaging() takes the head up to the first comma, semicolon or bracket, which keeps 'Regulator', so the class is 'reg?' and PACK_TEXT has no words for it
cause.subaru: name 'Motor Assembly-Regulator': the same head rule gives 'reg?' (the nissan pattern)

hash: positions.py is unchanged, so policy_sha256 is unchanged (71024c85add3...); the reading is in curate.py (ROUND10_NS = {mopar, subaru}, Curation._r10_class), which is not hashed. The other seven groups files (gm, toyota, ford, hmg, vag, mb, nissan) re-curate byte-identical.
rule: the kind of a window-regulator number is read from every naming field the raw prints for it: list rows on every page (main, aux) and product records (name, aux, description, other_names), each ';'-separated value on its own, each with site:lists|records:L<line>. A name is 'regulator+motor' (motor and/or & regulator, regulator with motor), 'motor' (starts with motor / window motor / power window motor, or says window motor, regulator motor, motor assembly), 'regulator', or says neither. Names that disagree in kind (motor beside regulator or regulator+motor) hold the group (held_name_disagree), on mopar, subaru and nissan. Otherwise as round 10: a motor class (name / aux heads) gains 'window motor only; ' on the finished note and nothing else changes.

nissan.note: 79 window-regulator groups re-read with every naming field: no number's names disagree in kind; nissan.json is unchanged
